mana.headline: Front Attack Damage Boost first, then Weapon Damage Boost or Critical Damage Boost.

lines.note: A multiplier of its own, and about 63% of your boss damage lands from the front. Manastones, the Varian Genus board and Fury give it; no Soul Binding line or wing does.
Either of these two as the next pick.
Either of these two as the next pick.

mana.fill: Fill the other slots with Attack, then Critical Hit. For a hard tanking fight, one source puts Block first, then Defense and HP, because Block raises parry and shield block chance. The Templar guide itself takes damage lines first.
mana.pvp: Abyssal Manastones swap about a third of every roll for PvP lines such as PvP Attack. Use them only on a PvP set. Builds split on which PvP line to take first, so check what your Abyss gear already has.
extra: Only Superior and Superior Abyssal Manastones roll the damage lines, at 0.5% each per roll, so most of your slots will still be Attack, Critical Hit and the like.

pve.why: Lumiel's Interference is the only proc that slows how fast the target attacks (-50% Combat Speed, 7 s at Unique), which suits a tank. For a pure damage stone, Ulgorn's Will is the Templar favourite and every single-target stone of a grade averages the same.

pvp.why: A 2% chance to root, up to 5 s at Unique, once every 5 s at most. Nezekan's March holds a player in place.

theo.note: Templars mix damage and control among the top players, which fits a tank that has to hold enemies. The tier list names Ulgorn's Will as the most engraved damage stone.
